summary: Multi-account STS role chaining fails after org-policy rollout; CI job cannot assume prod debug role
description:
Issue summary: After an org-policy enforcement rollout on 2026-03-12 evening, our CI job that performs production debug deployments can no longer assume the cross-account debug role chain (CI -> ops-broker -> prod-deployer). Impact: Several Canary and hotfix deploys failed; on-call runbooks could not access prod nodes for investigation. Scope: affects ephemeral CI sessions originating from the ops project assuming roles in the prod account via an STS AssumeRoleChain pattern. Both AWS STS and GCP WIF chains were involved in the failing jobs.

Observed behaviour: assume-role returns AccessDenied with a Condition evaluation mentioning missing session tag 'env' on the role trust policy. On GCP, Workload Identity mappings began rejecting IAM impersonation for service-accounts that do not have the new 'deployment-namespace' attribute.

Immediate business impact: blocked P0/P1 diagnostics (internal only), slowed incident response for a customer-facing latency regression (linked incident recorded elsewhere).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger CI workflow 'ops/prod-debug-deploy' from ops project using ephemeral runner
3) ops-broker attempts to AssumeRole into prod-deployer with session tags forwarded
4) AWS returns AccessDenied: "Not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource arn:aws:iam::1111111111:role/prod-deployer with Condition evaluation failed: Required tag 'env' missing"

5) On parallel GCP path, CI runner exchanges OIDC token for Service Account impersonation and receives 403: 'Permission denied: serviceAccountTokenCreator' for service accounts missing 'deployment-namespace' attribute in WIF mapping.
logs: 2026-03-12T22:03:11Z | sts.amazonaws.com | AssumeRole failed | Caller: ci-runner-ops | Target: arn:aws:iam::1111111111:role/prod-deployer | Error: AccessDenied | Condition: MissingSessionTag: env
2026-03-12T22:03:12Z | ops-broker | ForwardedTags: team=infra; note: env tag dropped during chained session (observed)

2026-03-12T22:03:15Z | gcp-iam | iamcredentials.projects.serviceAccounts.generateAccessToken | Caller: workload-identity-pool-ops | Error: 403 Permission denied: serviceAccountTokenCreator | Missing attribute: deployment-namespace
investigation_notes: 03/12 22:05 - Initial triage: Replayed CI job with verbose STS logging. Confirmed ops-broker received tags from CI runner but the second-hop AssumeRole shows no 'env' session tag in AWS CloudTrail event for the final AssumeRole call.

03/12 22:20 - Hypothesis: org-policy rollout introduced an org tag-normalizer Lambda that strips tags not explicitly allowed, which runs in the ops account and removed 'env' from session tags during tag propagation.

03/12 22:40 - Correlated GCP change: WIF mapping enforcement change merged 2026-03-12 21:58 (PR #ops/wing-1523) that now requires 'deployment-namespace' attribute on OIDC tokens for SA impersonation. CI runners did not emit this attribute yet.

03/12 23:05 - Tested manual AssumeRole via CLI with explicit --tags env=prod; observed success. Replayed chained assume with ops-broker and saw tag drop; ops-broker code path uses AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity in one branch which does not forward tags unless STS session name is propagated — mismatch found.
03/13 01:12 - Checked IAM role trust policies: prod-deployer has Condition: StringEquals: sts:TagKeys contains 'env' and Condition on tag 'env' == 'prod'. When tag missing, access denied as expected.

03/13 02:00 - Reproduced GCP failure by requesting token without 'deployment-namespace' claim; mapping rejects. Verified that runners under new image 'runner:2026-03-01' don't include the claim until image patching PR is deployed.
workaround: Short-term: 1) Manually trigger CI with explicit --tags env=prod passed to first AssumeRole call (ops-runner CLI path) which preserves the tag for the final hop. 2) For GCP paths, run a temporary service account token exchange using an admin SA that has serviceAccountTokenCreator as a stopgap. Both are manual and require codeowner approval.
proposed_remediation: 1) Roll back or patch the org tag-normalizer to whitelist 'env' for session tags for the ops-broker workflow; ensure tag forwarding is preserved during chained STS. 2) Patch CI runner image to include 'deployment-namespace' claim in its OIDC tokens and cut release. 3) Add integration test that simulates chained AssumeRole with tag propagation and a WIF mapping enforcement. 4) Update runbooks to include explicit retry path and automated mitigation playbook.
comments: 2026-03-12T23:30 - Diego Ramos: Reproduced the tag-drop locally when using the ops-broker assumeRole chain. Looks like the broker uses AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity which historically strips tag forwarding; need to confirm kernel of change after org rollout.

2026-03-13T00:05 - Priya Menon (security): Org-policy change was intended to prevent uncontrolled session tags. We can whitelist 'env' for trusted broker principals; I will open a change with sec-team for approval.
2026-03-13T01:45 - Aisha Patel: Applying manual workaround to unblock a single hotfix deploy per Diego's instructions; creating short-lived runbook steps in incident channel #incidents-prod.

2026-03-13T09:10 - Diego Ramos: Preparing a hotfix PR to the runner image to insert 'deployment-namespace' claim into OIDC tokens and a follow-up PR to add an automated integration test. Will link PRs when ready.
next_steps: 1) Security to approve 'env' whitelist for ops-broker in tag-normalizer (owner: Priya Menon).
2) Deploy runner image patch with 'deployment-namespace' claim and roll out to ops runners (owner: Diego Ramos).
3) Add test coverage for chained STS tag propagation in infra CI (owner: infra-test-team).
4) After fixes, run an end-to-end verification and close ticket (owner: Aisha Patel).
